topic: How Fees and Expenses Affect Your Investment Portfolio
source_evidence: When acting as a principal, the broker-dealer generally will be compensated by selling the security to you at a price that is higher than the market price (the difference is called a markup), or by buying the security from you at a price that is lower than the market price (the difference is called a markdown).
question: Misconception: A broker-dealer can be compensated only by charging a commission when acting as your agent. Is that always true?
answer: No. A broker-dealer may also act as a principal by buying from or selling to you securities held in its own inventory. In that case, it is generally compensated through a markup when it sells to you above the market price, or a markdown when it buys from you below the market price.
